name: Descending thoracic aorta
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Continuation of the aortic arch (arch and its great vessels are Stage 3/neck territory, not modeled here); runs in the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral bodies, passing through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm to become the abdominal aorta.

name: Celiac trunk
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Foregut supply; a short (~1-2cm) midline trunk arising just below the aortic hiatus, classically dividing into three terminal branches.

name: Common hepatic artery
supplies_or_drains: liver (visceral organ, aggregate -- outside NMSK scope, see docs/ROADMAP.md Stage 4)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Continues as the proper hepatic artery (to the liver) and gives off the gastroduodenal artery; full hepatobiliary branching is visceral-organ detail outside this atlas's neuro-musculo-skeletal scope (see docs/ROADMAP.md Stage 4).

name: Splenic artery
supplies_or_drains: spleen (visceral organ, aggregate -- outside NMSK scope)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Tortuous course along the superior border of the pancreas to the spleen; visceral detail outside NMSK scope.

name: Left gastric artery
supplies_or_drains: stomach (visceral organ, aggregate -- outside NMSK scope)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Smallest celiac branch, to the lesser curvature of the stomach; visceral detail outside NMSK scope.

name: Superior mesenteric artery
supplies_or_drains: midgut (visceral organs, aggregate -- outside NMSK scope)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Midgut supply (distal duodenum through proximal 2/3 transverse colon); modeled as a single stub node -- full jejunal/ileal/colic arcade branching is visceral-organ detail outside this atlas's scope (see docs/ROADMAP.md Stage 4).

name: Gonadal artery (right) (testicular/ovarian)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Arises from the anterior abdominal aorta just below the renal arteries and descends retroperitoneally; long, thin vessel (testicular a. continues into the inguinal canal/scrotum, ovarian a. into the pelvis) regardless of sex-specific downstream anatomy.

name: Median sacral artery

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Internal iliac artery (right)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Pelvic supply; principal source of blood to the pelvic floor and perineum.

name: Superior gluteal artery (right)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Largest branch of the internal iliac; exits the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen above piriformis.

name: Inferior gluteal artery (right)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Exits through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, alongside the sciatic nerve.

name: Internal pudendal artery (right)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Principal arterial supply of the perineum and external genitalia; runs with the pudendal nerve through Alcock's canal.

name: Obturator artery (right)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4-5; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
notes: Exits through the obturator foramen; anastomoses variably with the medial circumflex femoral artery (an 'accessory/aberrant obturator artery' from the inferior epigastric is a well-documented, surgically important normal variant).
